season.name: Fall
season.line: What did the year produce, what does it owe, and who will share the bread?

movement.name: The Ingathering
movement.line: Rejoice, and leave the corners for the poor.

days.t: Leave the edges of your field
x: And when ye reap the harvest of your land, ye shall not complete the reaping of your field with exactness, and thou shalt not gather that which falls from thy reaping.
And thou shalt not go over the gathering of thy vineyard, neither shalt thou gather the remaining grapes of thy vineyard: thou shalt leave them for the poor and the stranger: I am the Lord your God.

days.t: The sheaf you forgot is for the sojourner
x: And when thou shalt have reaped corn in thy field, and shalt have forgotten a sheaf in thy field, thou shalt not return to take it; it shall be for the stranger, and the orphan, and the widow, that the Lord thy God may bless thee in all the works of thy hands.

days.t: Pull out some handfuls for her
x: And she rose up to glean; and Booz charged his young men, saying, Let her even glean among the sheaves, and reproach her not.
And do ye by all means carry it for her, and ye shall surely let fall for her some of that which is heaped up; and let her eat, and glean, and rebuke her not.

days.t: He who has pity on the poor lends to the Lord
x: He that has pity on the poor lends to the Lord; and he will recompense to him according to his gift.

days.t: If you pour yourself out for the hungry
x: and [if] thou give bread to the hungry from thy heart, and satisfy the afflicted soul; then shall thy light spring up in darkness, and thy darkness [shall be] as noon-day:
Now this: The one sowing sparingly will also reap sparingly, and the one sowing upon blessings will also reap upon blessings,
each as he has purposed in the heart, not out of grief or out of necessity. For God loves a cheerful giver.
And God [is] able to make all grace abound to you⁺, so that in every [way], always, having all sufficiency, you⁺ may abound to every good work.
